Maya Patel: Heads up — were seeing a weird resume/lease renegotiation loop when a client reconnects and the request gets routed to a different region. Customer app reports duplicate completion events and doubled billing traces. Repro steps below.

Saurav Iyer: Which canary? any logs?

Maya Patel: Canary `region-a-canary-2026-03-17` (rolled yesterday). I have a short log snippet where the client sends resume token, server accepts, then route flips, new region tries to `claim` lease, both sides think they own session:

```
[region-a] INFO resume accepted token=abc123 lease=claimed ttl=30
[region-b] WARN lease-claim conflict token=abc123 previous_owner=region-a
[region-a] INFO send: resume_ack
[region-b] INFO resume: accepted duplicate session id=xyz
```

Ben Cho: That explains the doubled usage. Metering pipeline dedup uses session id + owner, and when owner flips we end up double-reporting. Saw ~0.3% bump in resume-related billing for that tenant.

Alice Nguyen: Console UX also confusing — the session list shows two active connections for the same user for ~10s then one disappears. Product asked if we can surface "pending lease takeover" state instead of two actives.

Charlie Park: Quick idea: add a short-lived "lease-renegotiate" phase during resume where the new route must ask old owner to transfer, with an opt-in atomic handoff. If old owner is still live we forward the KV cache instead of creating duplicate session.

Saurav Iyer: That would avoid double metering. But how do we handle old owner being dead/unreachable? We need a fallback TTL so new owner can forcibly claim after Xs. Also need to prevent replay during that window.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Current behavior: new owner immediately accepts and publishes session claim. Old owner doesn't get explicit revoke, just times out. Leads to both emitting token usage.

deploy-bot: Deployed region-a-canary-2026-03-17 at 2026-03-17T18:22:31Z by @alice — route affinity change enabled for 5% of traffic.

Alice Nguyen: For Console, we can show a transient badge: "handoff in progress" and hide duplicate billing lines until handoff completes or TTL expires. That reduces user confusion and support noise.

Charlie Park: Proposed protocol sketch:

```
# on new owner
send: lease_request(token)
wait up to 2s for lease_transfer
if transfer arrives:
  adopt state, emit single resume_event(owner=new)
else:
  force_claim(owner=new), mark dedupe_window=30s
```

over old owner:
```
on lease_request(token):
  if active and can forward:
    send lease_transfer(state)
    mark session=transferred
  else:
    ignore -> new owner will force
```

Maya Patel: Two practical questions: 1) is 2s wait acceptable latency-wise? 2) how do we propagate this across proxy/prefetch layers (some proxies drop these messages)?

Saurav Iyer: 2s seems fine for resume path (clients expect <500ms for cold start but resume can be slower). For proxies, we'll need a routed control plane channel (opaque control header) or use our internal control bus (ops-bus). If proxies drop, new owner may time out and force claim — still safe.

Ben Cho: Metering change: mark resume events with a lease_owner canonical id and handshake_id. Billing dedupe should prefer handshake_id when present. If handshake not present, fallback to existing logic.

Maya Patel: I've got a short heap of unit logs showing difference between old/new behavior; filing a minimal repro in /tmp and will attach. For now can we throttle the canary and enable a temporary console filter to hide duplicates?

Alice Nguyen: Yes, I can add a console filter flag `hide-duplicate-resumes` that toggles per-org. Quick UI change — will ship behind feature flag.

Charlie Park: I'll prototype handshake messages in runtime; @Saurav you'll take the metering changes?

Saurav Iyer: Yep, I'll own metering dedupe + handshake_id. Est ETA: 3 days for backend changes, 2 days for tests.

Maya Patel: Action items:
- Charlie: prototype lease-handshake (runtime) — due EOW
- Saurav: billing dedupe + handshake_id (billing infra) — ETA 3 days
- Alice: console filter flag + transient badge — quick PR today
- Ben: monitor canary traffic, throttle if duplicate rate > 0.1%

Ben Cho: Will throttle to 1% of users on that canary and monitor. Posting alert rule: `resume_duplicate_rate > 0.001 -> pager` (low severity).

ops-bot: Incident note recorded in #incidents (ref: INC-2026-034).

Maya Patel: Thanks team — I'll put the repro and raw logs in the ticket and follow up with a design doc once Charlie has the prototype. :thumbsup:
